adaptations.reason: R1 rule 1: noExplicitAny warn -> error. Plus the minimum mechanical changes needed for the copy to parse under @biomejs/biome 2.4.16, which is the 2.x line Canon's own package.json declares: organizeImports -> assist.actions.source.organizeImports, files.ignore -> negated files.includes, a11y.useAriaProps -> a11y.useAriaPropsForRole, a11y.noBlankTarget -> security.noBlankTarget, suspicious.noRestrictedGlobals -> style.noRestrictedGlobals with an object-valued deniedGlobals map. See brain finding: Canon's canonical biome.json does not parse under ANY currently installable Biome, so this adaptation is mandatory, not stylistic.

Biome's noMisleadingCharacterClass rejects the canonical file: it puts U+FE0F and U+200D in the same character class as the emoji ranges, but those are combining/format characters and the pair forms one grapheme. Split into EMOJI_RE + COMBINING_RE with an identical detected code-point set. Also retargeted two messages that recommend lucide-react icons, which do not apply to a service with no UI.
C2: no Next.js. jsx/plugins/next paths removed; lib is ES2022, not dom.
R1 rule 6: adapter-duplication exemption is an ignore entry carrying a reason, not a convention. ignoreDependencies reduced to what this repo actually installs.
C5: Node environment instead of jsdom; the risky logic here is temporal and server-side. Canon's jsdom config is added as a second project when a UI exists.
project dictionary extended with calendar/Dolt vocabulary.
C4: migration directory re-pointed from supabase/migrations to migrations/.
C2: build job runs type-check instead of next build; accessibility.yml and e2e.yml recorded not-applicable rather than created empty.

canonAdaptation: Canon's canonical biome.json does not parse under any currently installable Biome (verified against 1.9.4, 2.4.16 and 2.5.15) even though Canon's own package.json declares @biomejs/biome ^2.4.0. S0 therefore carries the minimum mechanical renames needed to parse, each declared with its reason in scripts/canon-audit.mjs, and files the upstream defect as a canon-extension item rather than working around it silently.
